question.text: A convertible instrument used by AIFs:

answer.text: Can only be converted from equity to debt
Is an equity-linked instrument that can convert from debt securities or preference shares into equity shares
Is the same as a government bond
Cannot be used by Cat I AIFs

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook recognises equity-linked instruments convertible into equity shares, VCF latitude to use convertible structures, and venture debt/mezzanine with equity upside such as warrants. Conversion of convertible debentures/debt securities and preference shares into equity shares is also referenced in the tax treatment. The Trap: Conversion runs from debt or preference into equity, not the other way around. Convertibles are not government bonds, and Category I AIFs (including VCFs) do use them. Note: Earlier wording leaned heavily on downside protection, liquidation preference, negotiated trigger events, and a popular-in-VC/PE marketing line. Those specifics are not directly supported by the checked workbook and have been removed; the explanation now stays with the equity-linked conversion and equity-upside/mezzanine references.
